items.title: 71542_Bill Coleman autobiographical manuscript
items.q: We played in Jean Goldkette's famous Greystone Ballroom.

ctx.x: was impossible to sleep. I killed one or two and there must have been at least five hundred that came to their funeral.

We played Gron ton, Middletown, most of the mining towns, Columbus, Dayton and then went to Detroit where we played in Jean Goldkette's famous Greystone Ballroom. Lloyd must have really cleaned up that night because he gave us fifty dollars each, the most money I had ever made on a percentage job in one night. I had learned by now that Lloyd would really look after himself first on percentage jobs, so if he gave us fifty each, it was certain that he a Cecil had three times that much or more.

But I did not worry about that as long as he treated me fairly. He never paid us for the date we did at the park, after he had lost all the money and then winning it back took off for New York leaving us to get back the best way they could. We forgave him and forgot it in a manner.
